About Ha Giang Safari Hostel
Ha Giang Safari Hostel and Tour is a woman-owned, family-run hostel in Ha Giang City, specializing in small-group Ha Giang Loop motorbike tours and cozy, home-style accommodation for travelers exploring northern Vietnam. Learn more about our story and how Ha Giang Safari Hostel came into existence.
Book a tour now!
Tour information
THE STORY OF HA GIANG SAFARI — A HA GIANG LOOP TOUR COMPANY
2017 Where it Began
Leaving Hanoi Behind
At 22, Thảo was an accountant in Hanoi — successful but unfulfilled. Breaking free from corporate life and beauty-standard pressures, she left to find a more meaningful path. That decision eventually led her to Ha Giang.
2018 First Venture
A Homestay in Yen Minh
Thảo and her husband Tu arrived in Ha Giang with a shared dream. They welcomed their first daughter, Talia, and invested all of their wedding gift money into a small homestay in Yen Minh.
2019 Setback
COVID-19 Forces the First Closure
The worsening COVID-19 outbreak forced the homestay to close. Thảo and Tu said goodbye to their first venture — but not to their dream of building something in Northern Vietnam.
2020-2021 Resilience
Safari Home Opens Its Doors
While selling paint, bird's nest, and clothing to support her family, Thảo pitched a bold idea: a hostel in Ha Giang — at the peak of COVID-19, with limited money and a newborn.
"We will either win everything or lose everything."
Safari Home opened with just enough money to buy eight motorbikes. The risk paid off.
2022 Growing the Brand
Recognised as a Ha Giang Loop Tour Company
With no staff and limited English, Thảo and Tu ran everything themselves. Thảo committed to learning English through online videos and volunteers — knowing communication was key to Safari's future.
2023 International Reach
Welcoming the World to Ha Giang
Safari began to truly thrive, welcoming travellers from across the globe to explore the breathtaking landscapes of Northern Vietnam on the famous Ha Giang Loop.
2024 New Chapter
Ha Giang Safari Hostel Opens
Thảo welcomed her second daughter, baby Linda, and expanded with a new location — Ha Giang Safari Hostel — cementing Safari's place as a leading Ha Giang travel experience.
Today Our Mission
The Safari Family Lives On
Safari's values remain unchanged: welcoming travellers to feel the magic of the Ha Giang Loop, creating unforgettable memories, and supporting the local community and children in need.
“About the name of Ha Giang Safari… a lot of people ask why I name the business “Safari” and the answer is really simple. I have an iPhone and I click on Safari to look and ask for anything I need. So I hope the people can understand when they come to Safari, you can find everything you need.”

Ultimate Guide to the Ha Giang Loop 2026​
Route, Itineraries, Tips & Maps
The Hà Giang Loop is Vietnam’s most breathtaking motorbike of adventure. This complete guide covers routes, itineraries, maps, safety tips, and everything you need to know before you go.
Book tour with Safari
What is the Ha Giang Loop?
The Ha Giang Loop Vietnam is a stunning 350km motorbike route in the far north of the country, starting and ending in Ha Giang City. It is widely considered the greatest motorbike loop in Vietnam, taking travelers through the UNESCO-recognized Dong Van Karst Plateau Global Geopark and traversing massive peaks like the Ma Pi Leng Pass. A typical Ha Giang Loop tour takes 3 to 4 days to complete and is famous for its dramatic limestone cliffs, deep canyons, vibrant ethnic minority villages, and winding mountain roads that challenge even experienced riders.
Feature
Detail
🏁 Distance
350km - 400km
⏳ Duration
2 Days (Fast), 3 Days, or 4 Days (Recommended)
☀️ Best Time
September–November (Harvest) & March–May (Spring)
🛣️ Road Condition
Paved but uneven mountain roads with steep passes, sharp turns, occasional potholes, and unpredictable road conditions
Best Time to Do the Ha Giang Loop
Ha Giang is beautiful all year, but the experience changes a lot depending on the season. Knowing when to go and what to expect each month can help you plan the safest and most scenic ride.
Autumn (September – November): Golden Fields & Ideal
Fall is often considered the  best season  to do the Ha Giang Loop, especially for travelers who want the most reliable weather. The skies are usually clear, the temperatures are pleasant, and the roads are smoother and safer than in the rainy months. September and October are famous for golden rice terraces, making this one of the most photogenic times of year in Ha Giang.
Winter (December – January): Cold, Quiet & Atmospheric
Winter in Ha Giang is cold, peaceful, and dramatic. Temperatures drop significantly in the mountains, especially at night. Early mornings can be misty or foggy, creating a magical atmosphere with quiet roads that feel more local. The Ha Giang Loop in winter is perfect for travelers who want a calmer experience and don’t mind bundling up. Bring warm layers, gloves, and a windproof jacket.
Spring (February – April): Cool, Clear & Colorful
Spring is one of the best times to do the Ha Giang Loop because the weather is comfortable and the scenery feels alive. Days are usually warm but not too hot, and mornings can be cool and fresh. The mountains are green, flowers begin to bloom, and you’ll get beautiful views without the intense heat of summer. This season is perfect for travelers who want great road conditions, clear photos, and a balanced mix of sunshine and light mountain breeze.
Summer (May – August): Lush Green & Rainy
Summer in Ha Giang is the most vibrant season for landscapes. The rice fields and mountains turn a deep green, waterfalls are full, and everything looks wild and tropical. However, this is also the rainy season, so you can expect sudden rain showers, slippery roads, and occasional fog in the mountains. It’s still an amazing time to ride the Ha Giang Loop if you’re okay with unpredictable weather.

Our most popular tour! Our 4-day tour has the most views, cultural immersion, and the best way to fully experience the Ha Giang Loop.

Ultimate 4-Day Ha Giang Loop Itinerary
DAY 1
Ha Giang to Yen Minh (Gateway to the Loop)
Start in Ha Giang City and ride through Bac Sum Pass to Heaven Gate , stopping in Tam Son (Quan Ba) , exploring Lung Khuy Cave , and finishing the day with views of the Yen Minh pine hills before overnighting in Yen Minh Town .
DAY 2
Yen Minh to Dong Van (The Northern Peaks)
Depart Yen Minh Town and ride the winding Tham Ma Pass , visit the historic H’mong King Palace , head up to the iconic Lung Cu Flag Point , and end the day in Dong Van Town for the night.
DAY 3
Dong Van to Du Gia (The highlight of the Ha Giang tour)
Leave Dong Van Town and ride the legendary Ma Pi Leng Pass , cruise along the stunning Nho Que River , pass through Meo Vac Town and Mau Due , then finish the day in peaceful Du Gia Village for the night.
DAY 4
Du Gia to Ha Giang (Waterfall & Culture)
Wake up in Du Gia and stop at Tham Luong Waterfall. R ide through Tham Luong Village , Duong Thuong , and Lung Tam Village , passing Thuan Hoa before arriving back in Ha Giang City to complete your loop adventure.
Ha Giang Loop & Cao Bang Map
The Ha Giang Loop is a true circular route that brings you back to Ha Giang City, while the Cao Bang route is a more undiscovered Northern Vietnam adventure with quieter roads and hidden gems.
Should You Self-Drive or Book an Easy Rider?
Deciding how to experience this Ha Giang Loop tour is crucial for safety and enjoyment.
Easy Rider (Guided Ha Giang Tour)
The safest and most popular option.
Sit behind a skilled, licensed local guide. You get all the thrill and views of the Ha Giang Loop Vietnam without the stress of navigating dangerous cliff-side roads and oncoming trucks.
VS.
Self-Drive (DIY)
Only for experienced riders confident on manual or semi-automatic bikes in all types of road conditions. Police checkpoints are common in Ha Giang City, and unlicensed bikes can be confiscated. ⚠️ Warning : You must have a valid IDP (International Driving Permit) with a clear motorcycle endorsement to legally ride on a Ha Giang motorbike tour.

Cao Bang, Vietnam: Travel Guide & Cao Bang Loop Tours
Cao Bang is a remote province in northern Vietnam known for limestone mountains, borderland scenery, and natural landmarks like Ban Gioc Waterfall, offering travelers a quiet and scenic alternative to Vietnam’s more popular motorbike routes.
Book tour with Safari
Why Visit Cao Bang?
Cao Bang is perfect for travelers who want to slow down and explore a side of Vietnam most tourists never reach.
With peaceful backroads, emerald rivers, ethnic minority villages, and dramatic natural sights, the region feels raw, authentic, and deeply connected to nature.
Unlike the Ha Giang Loop, Cao Bang is less about adrenaline and more about immersion. It s fewer crowds, more driving, and time to connect with the landscape and local culture.
✨ At Ha Giang Safari Hostel & Tour , we offer Cao Bang as a standalone journey or as an extension after the Ha Giang Loop, designed for travelers who want to go deeper into northern Vietnam, not just pass through it.
Historic Beauty
Lenin Stream is a serene Cao Bang landmark where Ho Chi Minh lived and worked in 1941, known for its turquoise waters, limestone scenery, and deep historical significance near Pac Bo Cave.
Iconic Sights
Angel Eye Mountain is one of Cao Bang’s most unique natural sights, famous for its massive limestone peak with a circular “eye” opening, set amid quiet valleys and rice fields.
Shhh...it's a secret!
Cao Bang is full of hidden gems that most travelers in Vietnam never see. This is where we come in , guiding you beyond the highlights and into authentic landscapes.
Feature
Detail
📍 Location
Cao Bang is a mountainous province in northern Vietnam, bordering China.
🚐 Distance & Access
About 280 km from Hanoi (7–8 hours by road). Often combined with the Ha Giang Loop.
☀️ Best Time
If waterfalls are your priority, visit from June to October. If weather and road conditions matter most, March–May and September–October offer the best balance.
✨ Why Cao Bang Is Special
Less touristy than Ha Giang, strong mix of nature + history, ideal for slow travel, perfect for small-group, motorbike, jeep, or car tours
Ban Gioc Waterfall (Vietnam’s Most Beautiful Waterfall)
Ban Gioc Waterfall is the largest natural waterfall in Vietnam and one of the most impressive in Southeast Asia. Sitting directly on the Vietnam–China border, it spans multiple tiers with powerful cascades surrounded by lush rice fields and limestone cliffs.
Best time to visit:
September–October (full flow, green fields)
March–May (clear water, fewer crowds)
Book tour with Safari
Best Time to Visit Cao Bang
Cao Bang can be visited year-round, but your ideal time to visit depends on whether you’re chasing waterfalls, clear skies, rice fields, or quiet roads.
Autumn (September – October): Best overall season
Autumn is widely considered the best time to visit Cao Bang . The weather is stable, skies are clearer, and rice fields turn golden across the valleys. Water levels remain strong, but crowds are still relatively low.
Best for: Overall best conditions, scenery, and road quality
Winter (November – February): Cool, misty, peaceful
Winter in Cao Bang is cooler and quieter. Mist often settles in the valleys, creating a moody, peaceful atmosphere. Waterfalls are calmer, and the region feels more remote — perfect for travelers who enjoy solitude and slower travel.
Best for: Fewer tourists, peaceful landscapes, cultural immersion Note: Bring warm layers, especially at night
Spring (March – May): Flowers, mild weather
Spring is one of the most comfortable times to visit Cao Bang. Temperatures are mild, the landscape is fresh and green, and flowers bloom across the valleys. Waterfalls begin to flow again after winter, making this a great balance of scenery and pleasant riding conditions.
Best for: Comfortable weather, photography, cultural exploration
Summer (June – August): Lush landscapes, waterfalls full
Summer brings lush greenery and powerful waterfalls, especially at Ban Gioc Waterfall , which is at its most dramatic during this time. Occasional rain showers are common, but they also bring life to the rivers, rice fields, and forests.
Best for: Waterfalls, vibrant landscapes, adventurous travelers Note: Roads can be slippery after heavy rain
Ha Giang Loop & Cao Bang Map
The Ha Giang Loop is a true circular route that starts and ends in Ha Giang City. Cao Bang, while often referred to as a “loop,” is actually a point-to-point journey on the map.
Cao Bang vs Ha Giang: What’s the Difference?
Whether you choose one route or combine both into a single journey, understanding the differences will help you plan the adventure that fits your travel style best.
